name: Valle Nacional Chinantec
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only classification refs (Merrifield 1994, Campbell 2017) found; SIL Mexico page 403/404; no phonology located

sources.citation: Silverman, Daniel. 2006. Chinantec: Phonology. In K. Brown (ed.), Encyclopedia of Language and Linguistics, 2nd ed., 211-213. Elsevier.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Family-level only: lists Valle Nacional among the 14 Chinantecan languages; 'Stem complexes are obligatorily stressed. Post-tonic and pre-tonic syllables are not stressed' (illustrated from Comaltepec/Sochiapan/Quiotepec). No VN-specific data.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record vall1253 (3 refs: Merrifield 1994 overview, Campbell 2017, Campbell et al. 2022 ELCat; classification: Chinantec Group III = Ozumacin [chz] + Valle Nacional [cvn]).
en.wikipedia 'Palantla Chinantec' (target of redirect 'Valle Nacional Chinantec') and 'Chinantecan languages'.
sources.note: Tertiary: treats 'the variety of San Mateo Yetla, known as Valle Nacional Chinantec' under Palantla; family article says roots obligatorily stressed, stress typically on final syllable of the root (citing Silverman 2006, Macaulay 1999, Foris 2000) -- not VN-specific.

sources.citation: Westley, David O. & William R. Merrifield. 1990. Moving and arriving in the Chinantla. In Merrifield & Rensch (eds.), Syllables, tone, and verb paradigms (Studies in Chinantec Languages 4), 107-130. Dallas: SIL/UTA.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only 'fragmentary evidence from Valle Nacional' on an animate suffix -ng (Google snippet + TOC scanned); nothing on stress.
